chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Thabit, the mawla of the family of Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Suppressing the anger from the enemy during their power, as a form of dissimulation (taqiyyah), is prudence for the one who practices it, and a protection from exposure to affliction in the world. And opposing the enemies during their power and confronting them without dissimulation is neglecting the Command of Allah. Therefore, be polite to the people, for that will nourish (increase your standing) for you in their presence, and do not make enemies of them, lest they carry you on their necks (dominate you) and you become humiliated.

key_terms.فَجَامِلُوا النَّاسَ: Therefore, be polite to the people

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on suppressing anger and showing politeness to enemies when they are in power?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between strategic patience (hazm) during the enemy's dominance, which preserves dignity, and reckless confrontation that leads to humiliation. This teaching emphasizes that 'jamila' (social grace) is a practical manifestation of taqiyyah, ensuring the Shia community remains respected rather than subservient. It reflects the historical context of early Shia communities navigating political pressures while maintaining religious integrity.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Sabit, a slave of the family of Hareyz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Supressing the anger from the enemies in their government by dissimulation is prudence for the one who takes by it, and is a protection from the exposure to the affliction in the world and the animosity of the enemies in their government, and opposition to them in their government without dissimulation is to neglect the Command of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. Therefore, pay compliments to the people, that would nourish for you in their presence, and do not make enemies out of them, so they would be riding upon your necks and humiliate you’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Thabit Mawla Ale Hariz from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

To suppress one’s anger in the face of the enemy, the ruling party’s government, for protection ( Taqiyah ), is a cutting edge for those who adopt it. It is to avoid being exposed to suffering in this world and to the animosity of the ruling party in their government. Opposition to such ruling parties without maintaining protective ( Taqiyah ) measures is ignoring the commands of Allah. Maintain a graceful position toward people; it will grow with them in your favor. Do not deal with them as your enemies; otherwise, you make them impose burdens on you and humiliate you.”
